Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (identity), Dev (runtime) and Laura for security sign-off. I attached a short checklist and the minimal networking text we usually give customers. Short answers up front:

- SAML assertions: yes — we can map custom attributes to control-plane IAM roles. We support attribute-to-role mapping and can apply precedence rules when SCIM groups also exist.
- SCIM: we support SCIM v2 with incremental sync (last-modified/delta) and pagination.
- Network: TLS outbound to our private control-plane endpoint on 443; we publish hostnames (and optional IP ranges) — see attached networking-ports.txt.
- Service account: SCIM token is scoped to user/group provisioning and service-account based tokens are recommended. We recommend rotating tokens on a schedule (see scim-token-rotation.md).

Attached: sso-scim-checklist.pdf, networking-ports.txt

Next step: Neha, can you confirm the exact SAML attribute names we prefer and any transform rules? Dev, please note the proxy option if Acme wants to avoid public egress. Laura — can you comment on minimum assurance for token rotation?

Cheers,

Hey all — quick technical note from identity side:

- SAML: We typically accept NameID (persistent) as the primary principal. For role mappings we prefer a dedicated attribute named "redwood_roles" (comma-separated) or the standard "roles" claim. We will also accept Okta's group-to-claim mapping if you want group names translated into role names.
- Transform rules: We support simple prefix/suffix and regex-based replacements in mapping rules (e.g., strip "ACME_" from group names).
- SCIM: Delta sync is based on lastModified and we support bulk pagination. Rate limits are soft (150 req/min for provisioning endpoints in Private deployments by default) but can be raised on request for initial syncs.

For SP metadata: we need the EntityID and ACS URL from your Okta app. If you can share the metadata XML or Okta app link, we’ll pre-populate mapping templates.

Hi Olivia — answering the SCIM token and network questions: 

- Tokens: SCIM service tokens are scoped. We create a dedicated provisioning scope that grants only user/group create/update/delete and read on the identity endpoints — it does not permit access to audit logs or other admin APIs.
- Rotation: we recommend rotating tokens every 90 days by default. For higher assurance customers we recommend 30-day rotation and support short-lived tokens (7–15 days) with an automated rotation hook.
- Network: outbound TLS to your Redwoods endpoint on 443. For fully private setups we can support an outbound proxy that routes traffic to Redwood’s private Egress Relay; this removes the need to open IP ranges.
- Role precedence: if both a SAML attribute and an SCIM group map to roles, our precedence rule is: explicit role attribute > SCIM group assignment > default role. We can make precedence configurable for the account.

Attached: scim-token-rotation.md

Let us know if you want an example Okta claim mapping or a sample metadata.xml and I’ll drop that in.
